title: 8. 笛卡尔、斯宾诺莎和莱布尼茨

zh: 8. 笛卡尔、斯宾诺莎和莱布尼茨
en: 8. Descartes, Spinoza and Leibniz

zh: 十八世纪伟大的爱尔兰剧作家理查德·谢里丹在他的一部喜剧中，让其中一个角色——一个老赌徒——说道：“我打牌从来不输——或者说，至少我从来不觉得自己在输，这其实是一回事。”当然，我们知道这两者并非一回事，正如认为自己有一百万英镑，与实际拥有这笔钱，也是截然不同的两回事。对大多数人来说，思想与存在是两回事，这是不言而喻的。但思想的本质究竟是什么？它与存在究竟有何关系？这些棘手的哲学问题，曾让那个时代一些最杰出的头脑为之苦思。
en: In one of his comedies, Richard Sheridan, the great Irish dramatist of the eighteenth century, makes one of his characters, an inveterate gambler, say: “I never lose at cards – or, at least, I never feel that I am losing, which is the same thing.” Of course, we know that it is not the same thing, just as it is not the same thing to think one has a million pounds, compared to actually possessing that amount of money. That thought and being are two different things is self-evident to most people. But what is the precise nature of thought? And what exactly is its relation to being? These were difficult philosophical questions, which exercised some of the most brilliant brains of the period.

zh: 尽管一些机械唯物主义者竭力证明思想是一种物质实体——就像胆汁由肝脏分泌出来一样，思想由大脑分泌出来——但思想本身是非物质的。思想是以特定方式组织起来的物质所具有的属性，但它本身并非物质。一旦思想开始发展，它便具有了某种独立的生命力，这种生命力随着劳动分工的发展和文明的进步而加速，而这一进程恰与社会阶级分化相吻合。思想本身成为了研究的对象。人们逐渐忽视了它的物质起源。它呈现为一种神秘的存在，与物质分离且独立，一种与上帝相连的神圣实体，一种不朽的灵魂，独立于我们的身体，即使我们死去，它也不会消亡。
en: Thought itself is immaterial, despite the efforts of some mechanical materialists to prove that it is a material substance, secreted by the brain, as bile is secreted from the liver. Thought is the property of matter organised in a particular way, but it is not itself matter. Once thought begins to develop, it takes on a certain life of its own, which proceeds more rapidly with the development of the division of labour and the growth of civilisation, which coincides with the division of society into classes. Thought itself becomes an object of study. Its material origins are lost sight of. It appears as something mystical, separate and apart from matter, a divine substance, linked to God, an immortal soul, independent of our body, which will not perish when we die.

zh: 由此产生了一个问题：如果思想与物质现实截然不同，为何它们却如此频繁地被发现是一致的？思想与存在之间的确切关系，在两年半间是所有主要哲学争论的根源，最终只有辩证唯物主义才对此给出了令人满意的解答。文艺复兴时期一种新型唯物主义的兴起，是科学在质上更高水平上重获新生的一项先决条件。但正如我们所见，这种唯物主义以经验主义的形式存在某种片面性，从而带来了极其负面的后果。人被视为单纯的观察者，其思想既与自身生活隔绝，也与外部世界隔绝。
en: The question arises, if thought and material reality are completely different, how does it happen that they are so often found to be in agreement? The exact relation between thought and being was the source of all the main philosophical disputes for two-and-a-half years, and was only resolved satisfactorily by dialectical materialism. The rise of a new kind of materialism in the period of the Renaissance was the prior condition for the rebirth of science on a qualitatively higher level. But, as we have seen, it suffered from a one-sidedness, in the form of empiricism, which had extremely negative consequences. Man was seen as a mere observer, and his thoughts as isolated from his life as well as the external world.
body.review: 所给英文原文作“two-and-a-half years”（两年半），与上下文所述的漫长哲学史不符，疑有脱词或排印错误。底稿译作“两千五百年”，但所给原文不足以确认这一补正；此处照录原文并提示。

zh: 否认一切非直接观察所得的结论的有效性，拒绝理论和广泛的概括（正如牛顿所言：“我不提出假说”），注定了这种唯物主义的贫瘠。主要结果是，这一学派的代表们无法超越当时科学世界观的局限——这种世界观在性质上本质上是机械的、静态的。这一缺陷不仅适用于英国经验主义者，甚至也适用于法国唯物主义者，尽管后者的视野要宽广得多，且偶尔在辩证法领域有过精彩的探索。
en: The denial of the validity of anything which did not come from immediate observation, the rejection of theory and broad generalisations (“I do not make hypotheses”, as Newton said) doomed this kind of materialism to sterility. The main result was that the representatives of this school could not rise above the limitations of the outlook of the science of the day, which was fundamentally mechanical and static in character. This defect applies not only to the English empiricists, but even to the French materialists, despite their far broader outlook and occasionally brilliant forays into dialectics.

zh: 旧唯物主义片面地理解人的思想，以静态、被动和直观的方式看待它。人只是在观察自然，记录“事实”。这种狭隘的唯物主义观念，虽然出发点是正确的，但最终却走入了死胡同，无法进一步发展。事实上，在马克思和恩格斯凭借其唯物辩证法理论带来革命性变革之前，唯物主义并未取得进一步的发展。就连费尔巴哈，其实也并未超越十八世纪的法国唯物主义者。
en: To the old materialism, human thought appeared one-sided and was considered in a static, passive and contemplative way. Man was merely observing nature, taking note of ‘the facts’. Setting out from a correct idea, this narrow conception of materialism ended up in a blind alley, incapable of further development. In fact, until the revolution effected by Marx and Engels, with their theory of materialist dialectics, no further development of materialism took place. Even Feuerbach really went no further than the French materialists of the eighteenth century.

zh: 因此，我们面临着哲学史上最大的悖论之一——洛克之后时期思想上的真正重大进步，并非由唯物主义者，而是由唯心主义者所实现。他们不受经验主义自我设限的束缚，得出一系列精彩的理论概括，尽管这些概括基于错误的假设，因而不可避免地带有幻想色彩。这一奇特现象在黑格尔的哲学中达到了极致——这是历史上最“巨大的失误”
——正如马克思所言，辩证法的所有主要要素虽以系统化的形式呈现，却完全倒置了。
en: We therefore come face to face with one of the greatest paradoxes in the history of philosophy – that the really significant advances in thought in the period after Locke were made, not by the materialists, but by the idealists. Unrestricted by the self-imposed limits of empiricism, they arrived at a whole series of brilliant theoretical generalisations, although, setting out from false hypotheses, they invariably had a fantastic character to them. This peculiar phenomenon reached its most extreme expression in the philosophy of Hegel, the most “colossal miscarriage”
in history, where all the main elements of dialectics appear in a systematic form, but standing on their head, as Marx put it.

zh: 关于思想与存在之间关系的问题，法国哲学家笛卡尔（1596—1650）提出的观点与英国经验主义者有所不同。他出生于一个中等富裕的家庭，曾师从耶稣会士。这种枯燥正统思想的熏陶，使他终生对任何形式的教条主义深恶痛绝，并对既有观念不耐烦。与休谟那种愤世嫉俗的悲观主义不同，他的怀疑主义具有生动而积极的特征。他开始怀疑的，并非知识的一般可能性，而仅仅是那些被当作无误真理提出的现有观点。从很小的时候起，他的座右铭就是：“对一切都持怀疑态度”。
en: The question of the relation of thought to being was posed by the French philosopher Descartes (1596-1650) in a different way to the English empiricists. Born into a moderately wealthy family, he had studied with the Jesuits. This taste of arid orthodoxy produced in him a lifetime’s aversion for dogmatism of any kind, and an impatience with received ideas. His scepticism, in contrast with the jaundiced pessimism of Hume, had a lively and positive character. He began to doubt, not the possibility of knowledge in general, but only the existing opinions put forward as infallible truths. From an early age, his motto was: ‘Doubt everything’.

zh: ……而且，由于我习惯于在每件事上都特别思考哪些内容可以合理地被怀疑、哪些可能成为错误的根源，我逐渐从脑海中根除了此前潜入的所有谬误。这并非说我在效仿那些仅为怀疑而怀疑、除了不确定性本身之外别无所求的怀疑论者；恰恰相反，我的目的仅在于寻找确信的依据，并剔除松散的泥土和沙砾，以便触及岩石或黏土。
en: …and, as I made it my business in each matter to reflect particularly upon what might fairly be doubted and prove a source of error, I gradually rooted out from my mind all the errors which had hitherto crept into it. Not that in this I imitated the sceptics who doubt only that they may doubt, and seek nothing beyond uncertainty itself; for, on the contrary, my design was singly to find ground of assurance, and cast aside the loose earth and sand, that I might reach the rock or the clay.

zh: 基于这些原因，一旦我的年龄允许我摆脱导师的管束，我就彻底放弃了书本学问的研究，并决心不再追求任何其他学问，只求认识自己，或是认识世界这本伟大的书。
en: For these reasons, as soon as my age permitted me to pass from under the control of my instructors, I entirely abandoned the study of letters, and resolved no longer to seek any other science than the knowledge of myself, or of the great book of the world.

zh: 为了获取知识并开阔眼界，他在三十年战争爆发之初先是加入了荷兰军队，随后又加入了巴伐利亚军队。还在军中服役时，他就写了一本哲学著作，但听说伽利略受审的消息后，他担心会激怒教会，便决定暂不出版。此后，他的著作中随处可见旨在安抚宗教当局、避免被指控为“无神论者”的措辞。即便如此，他仍像洛克一样，不得不迁居荷兰——这是欧洲唯一一个言论和写作氛围相对自由的国家。即便在这里，他仍面临宗教狂热分子（此处指新教徒）的攻击，他们指控他无神论。唯有奥兰治亲王的亲自干预，才使他免于被起诉。即便如此，莱顿大学当局仍对他实施全面禁令，甚至禁止提及他的名字。最终，他不得不迁居瑞典，并在那里去世，部分原因在于当地气候对其体弱多病的身体造成了影响。
en: In order to gain knowledge and expand his horizons he enlisted, first in the Dutch, and then the Bavarian army, at the start of the Thirty Years War. While still in the army, he wrote a book on philosophy, but, on hearing of the trial of Galileo, he decided to withhold publication for fear of provoking the anger of the Church. Later on, his writings appear liberally sprinkled with references aimed at placating the religious authorities and averting the dreadful charge of godlessness. Even so, like Locke, he felt obliged to move to the Netherlands, the only country in Europe where there existed a relatively free atmosphere to speak and write. Even here he faced the attacks of religious bigots (in this case, Protestants), who accused him of atheism. Only the personal intervention of the Prince of Orange saved him from prosecution. Even then, the authorities of the University of Leiden placed him under a total ban, forbidding the very mention of his name. Eventually, he had to move to Sweden, where he died, partly because of the effects of the climate on his weak constitution.

zh: 尽管笛卡尔极有可能是个信徒，但阅读他的著作时，人们会觉得他仿佛时刻都在提心吊胆。为了绕过教会的束缚，笛卡尔承认上帝的存在，但随即又表示，宗教是一个过于崇高的主题，不应“交由我们无力的理性来判断”。在探讨自然史时，他承认上帝创造了世界，但随后又仿佛在提出假设般补充道：
en: While in all probability Descartes was a believer, when reading his works, one has the impression of a man all the time looking over his shoulder. In order to get round the Church, Descartes accepts the existence of God, but then says that religion is too lofty a subject to be “submitted to the impotency of our reason.” When dealing with natural history, he accepts that God created the world, but then adds, as if hypothetically:

zh: 可以相信——这并不贬损创造奇迹的意义——仅仅通过这种方式，纯粹物质的事物就可能随着时间的推移，逐渐演变为我们所观察到的模样；当人们看到万物以这种方式逐渐产生时，其本质要比仅将其视为瞬间产生于一种完备且完美的状态时，更容易被理解。
en: [I]t may be believed, without discredit to the miracle of creation, that, in this way alone, things purely material might, in course of time, have become such as we observe them at present; and their nature is much more easily conceived when they are beheld coming in this manner gradually into existence, than when they are only considered as produced at once in a finished and perfect state.

zh: 这位最伟大的法国哲学家为了发表自己的思想，不得不诉诸这些迂回手段。
en: To such subterfuges did the greatest French philosopher have to resort in order to publish his ideas.

zh: 笛卡尔与科学
en: DESCARTES AND SCIENCE

zh: 笛卡尔是理性主义与经验主义之争、演绎法与归纳法之争的主要代表人物之一。英国人罗杰·培根是经验主义和归纳推理法的奠基人，该方法试图仅从观察到的事实中推导出理论。对培根而言，对观察的痴迷最终酿成了悲剧；他因早期一项将雪塞进鸡腹中的制冷实验而患上支气管炎，最终因此去世。
en: Descartes is one of the main protagonists in the struggle between rationalism and empiricism, between the method of deduction as opposed to that of induction. The Englishman Roger Bacon was the father of empiricism and the method of inductive reasoning, which attempts to derive theories from observed facts alone. In Bacon’s case, the obsession with observation proved fatal; he died of bronchitis as a result of an early experiment in refrigeration, involving stuffing a chicken with snow.
body.review: 原文写“Roger Bacon”（罗杰·培根），但随后以雪填鸡、试验冷藏而致病的叙述指向弗朗西斯·培根，与本书第七章所论人物也相应。此处保留原文人名，并提示混用。

zh: 理性主义者则从截然相反的立场切入科学，而笛卡尔更关注一般原理，而非具体的观察工作。他以欧几里得几何学为范本，试图发展出一套源于纯粹理性的、自洽且连贯的定理体系，而不依赖于不可靠的感官证据。理性主义成为法国的主流思潮，而培根的经验主义则在英吉利海峡对岸大获全胜。这两位学者虽以不同方式，却都推动了科学事业的发展，并都取得了重要的发现。
en: The rationalists approached science from a diametrically opposite standpoint, and Descartes was more concerned with general principles than the detailed work of observation. Taking Euclid’s geometry as his model, he attempted to develop consistent and coherent theorems derived from pure reason, without recourse to the unreliable evidence of the senses. Rationalism became the main tradition in France, whereas Bacon’s empiricism triumphed on the other side of the Channel. Both men, in different ways, advanced the cause of science, and both made important discoveries.

zh: 笛卡尔对科学的贡献卓尔不凡，尤其在数学领域，他可被视为解析几何的奠基人之一。他最伟大的贡献是发明了“坐标几何”，该理论通过点与两条固定直线的距离来确定该点在平面上的位置。在物理学方面，正如马克思和恩格斯所指出的，他是一位唯物主义者：
en: Descartes’ contribution to science was outstanding, especially in the field of mathematics, where he may be considered one of the founders of analytical geometry. His great contribution was the invention of ‘coordinate geometry’, which determines the position of a point in a plane by its distance from two fixed lines. In physics, he was a materialist, as Marx and Engels point out:

zh: 笛卡尔在他的物理学中赋予物质以自我创造的力量，并将机械运动视为其生命的表现。他将物理学与形而上学完全分离。在他的物理学中，物质是唯一的实体，是存在和知识的唯一基础。
en: Descartes in his physics endowed matter with self-creative power and conceived mechanical motion as the manifestation of its life. He completely separated his physics from his metaphysics. Within his physics, matter is the sole substance, the sole basis of being and of knowledge.

zh: 然而，笛卡尔未能解决思想与存在之间关系的根本问题。在他著名的《谈谈方法》中，他寻求一种人人都能接受且无可置疑的真理。他提出了那句名言：“我思故我在。”
这是他哲学的基石。然而，这一结论并不能由此前提推出。他至多只能断言：“我思，故思想存在。”这个“我”究竟是什么？显然，是人类的神经系统、大脑、身体等等。法国唯物主义者伽森狄提出异议，认为同样可以从人类的任何其他功能推导出存在。唯心主义者则反驳说，如果没有思想，就无法感知这些功能中的任何一种。但同时也必须阐明思想的本质。
en: Yet Descartes was unable to resolve the fundamental question of the relation between thought and being. In his celebrated Discourse on Method, he searches for a truth which everyone can accept as unquestionable. He comes up with the famous phrase: “I think, therefore I am.”

This is the cornerstone of his philosophy. And yet, it does not follow. At most he could assert, “I think, therefore thought exists.” What is this ‘I’? Evidently, a human nervous system, a brain, a body, and so on. Gassendi, the French materialist, objected that existence may equally well be inferred from every other human function. Idealists replied that none of these functions can be perceived without thought. But it is also necessary to say what thought is.

zh: 从一致的唯物主义立场来看，思想就是会思考的物质。它不会也不可能脱离物质而独立存在。在这个决定性的问题上，笛卡尔采取了一种令人不满意且自相矛盾的立场，最终导致了各种矛盾。他说，思想与物质之间的根本区别在于：物质具有广延，而思想、精神和灵魂则没有。这直接将我们引向二元论的立场。根据笛卡尔的观点，思想与物质之间没有任何共同之处。它们不仅不同，而且截然对立。因此，灵魂与身体的结合完全是一种机械性的结合。灵魂作为一种异物栖居于身体之中，这是一种机械的、完全人为的关系。没有灵魂，身体就像一台没有生命的机器或自动机。即使构造最精良的机器人也无法获得人类的意识，即使它被编程为能够说话（这段文字写于1637 年，但其主题却非常现代）。
en: Thought, from a consistent materialist position, is matter that thinks. It does not and cannot exist by itself, separate from matter. On this decisive question, Descartes adopted an unsatisfactory and inconsistent position, which ended up in all kinds of contradictions. The fundamental difference between thought and matter, he said, was that matter had extension, whereas thought, spirit and soul had none. This leads us straight to a dualist position. According to Descartes, there is nothing in common between thought and matter. They are not only different, but diametrically opposed. The union of soul and body is, therefore, an entirely mechanical one. The soul inhabits the body as an alien thing, a mechanical and entirely artificial relationship. Without the soul, the body is like a lifeless machine or automaton. Even the best-constructed robot cannot acquire a human consciousness, even if it is programmed to speak (this was written in 1637, but the subject matter is very modern).

zh: 例如，一台机器可以被教导说话，甚至表达“情感”：
en: For example, a machine may be taught to speak and even express ‘feelings’:

zh: ［但］它无法像智力水平最低的人那样，灵活地组织语言，以恰如其分地回应当面所说的话。第二个检验标准是：尽管此类机器在执行许多事务时，其完美程度可能与我们任何人相当甚至更胜一筹，但它们无疑会在某些其他事务上失败，由此便可发现它们并非基于知识行事，而是完全依赖其器官的运作方式；因为理性是一种普适的工具，在任何场合都能同样发挥作用，而这些器官却恰恰相反，每项具体行动都需要特定的安排；因此，就实际可能性而言，任何机器都不可能拥有足够多样化的器官，使其能够像我们的理性使我们能够那样，在生活中的一切情境中采取行动。
en: [B]ut not that it should arrange them variously so as appositely to reply to what is said in its presence, as men of the lowest grade of intellect can do. The second test is, that although such machines might execute many things with equal or perhaps greater perfection than any of us, they would, without doubt, fail in certain others from which it could be discovered that they did not act from knowledge, but solely from the disposition of their organs: for while reason is an universal instrument that is alike available on every occasion, these organs, on the contrary, need a particular arrangement for each particular action; whence it must be morally impossible that there should exist in any machine a diversity of organs sufficient to enable it to act in all the occurrences of like, in the way in which our reason enables us to act.
body.review: 引文的“morally impossible”在此指实际上不可能，不是道德上不允许。英文末尾作“occurrences of like”，疑为“life”的排印误差，中文依语境译作“生活中的一切情境”。

zh: 低等动物之所以被归类为“自动机”，正是出于同样的理由。值得较长地引用这段文字，因为它展现了一种鲜明的唯物主义论证思路，而且无疑远胜于当今某些科学家所谈论的神秘主义胡言乱语：
en: The lower animals are classed as “automata” for the same reason. It is worth quoting this passage at some length because it shows a markedly materialist line of argument, and certainly is vastly superior to the mystical nonsense talked by some scientists today:

zh: 因为值得特别注意的是，没有哪个人——哪怕是白痴——会愚钝到无法将不同的词语组合起来，从而构建出一种能表达其思想的陈述；而另一方面，没有任何其他动物——无论多么完美或处境多么优越——能够做到这一点。这种无能并非源于器官的缺失：因为我们观察到，喜鹊和鹦鹉虽能像我们一样发出词语，却无法像我们那样说话，即无法表明它们理解自己所说的话；相反，那些先天聋哑的人，虽然比野兽更缺乏他人用于说话的器官，却习惯于自发地发明某些手势，借此向那些通常与他们相处、且有闲暇学习其语言的人表达自己的思想。这不仅证明了兽类比人类理智更少，而且证明它们根本没有理智：因为我们看到，要使一个人能够说话，所需的条件非常少；而且既然在同一种类的动物中，正如在人类中一样，可以观察到某种能力上的差异，而且有些个体比其他个体更容易接受教导，那么，除非野兽的灵魂本质上与我们的灵魂截然不同，否则很难相信，同种中最完美的猿猴或鹦鹉，在这一点上竟不能与人类中最愚蠢的婴儿，或者至少与一个脑子有问题的婴儿相提并论。
en: For it is highly deserving of remark, that there are no men so dull and stupid, not even idiots, as to be incapable of joining together different words, and thereby constructing a declaration by which to make their thoughts understood; and that on the other hand, there is no other animal, however perfect or happily circumstanced, which can do the like. Nor does this inability arise from want of organs: for we observe that magpies and parrots can utter words like ourselves, and are yet unable to speak as we do, that is, so as to show that they understand what they say: in place of which men born deaf and dumb, and thus not less, but rather more than the brutes, destitute of the organs which others use in speaking, are in the habit of spontaneously inventing certain signs by which they discover their thoughts to those who, being usually in their company, have leisure to learn their language. And this proves not only that the brutes have less reason than man, but that they have none at all: for we see that very little is required to enable a person to speak; and since a certain inequality of capacity is observable among animals of the same species, as well as among men, and since some are more capable of being instructed than others, it is incredible that the most perfect ape or parrot of its species, should not in this be equal to the most stupid infant of its kind, or at least to one that was crack-brained, unless the soul of brutes were of a nature wholly different from ours.

zh: 笛卡尔的唯心主义使他陷入了将心灵与身体割裂的陷阱，并将身体视为一个单纯的自动机，灵魂就栖居于其中。这成为一种相当大的困惑之源，并对科学界对心灵真实本质及其与身体、大脑和神经系统之间关系的理解产生了有害影响。
en: Descartes’ idealism led him into the trap of dividing mind from body, and regarding the body as a mere automaton, inside which the soul dwelt. This became a source of considerable confusion, and had a harmful effect on the scientific understanding of the real nature of the mind and its relation to the body, the brain and the nervous system.

zh: 尽管《谈谈方法》一书总体上带有唯心主义倾向，但笛卡尔的唯物主义物理学和生物学思想却不断渗透其中。例如，他无法掩饰自己对哈维发现血液循环这一成果的热情，为此他专门用了不下六页的篇幅。然而，当涉及心与身关系这一棘手问题时，他却退守于非科学且形而上的概念之中。他将灵魂定位于大脑中央所谓的“松果体”中，纯粹是因为大脑的其他部分都是成对存在的，因此不具备作为灵魂器官的资格——否则灵魂恐怕会因此患上严重的复视症！
en: Despite the generally idealist thrust of the Discourse, Descartes’ materialist physics and biology keep on intruding. He cannot, for example, conceal his enthusiasm for Harvey’s discovery of the circulation of the blood, to which he dedicates no fewer than six pages. Yet when he comes to the vexed question of the relationship of mind and body, he takes refuge in unscientific and metaphysical concepts. He locates the soul in the so-called ‘pineal gland’ in the centre of the brain, purely because all the other parts of the brain are double, and therefore disqualified from acting as the organ of the soul, which would thereby presumably end up with a bad case of double-vision!

zh: 这一切的问题在于：如果思想与物质被视为完全分离的，那么它们又是通过何种方式结合并维系在一起的呢？笛卡尔唯一可行的选择是引入一个外部作用者——即神的干预。即便如此，也无法理解它们如何能相互影响。它们究竟通过何种机制相互渗透？例如，心灵可以意愿我抬起手臂，但它如何才能真正地抬起手臂呢？笛卡尔的弟子赫林克斯以令人钦佩的坦率回答说，心灵无法做到这一点，我的手臂恰好在我意愿的同时抬起，这纯属巧合。这凸显了笛卡尔哲学的矛盾之处——即未解决的二元论，这也是其致命弱点。
en: The problem with all this is that, if thought and matter are considered as completely separate, by what means are they united and kept together? The only option open to Descartes was to bring in an external agent – divine intervention. Even so, it is impossible to see how they can have any effect upon each other. By what mechanism could they interpenetrate? For example, the mind can will that I lift my arm, but how can it actually lift it? Descartes’ disciple, Geulinx, answered with admirable frankness that it could not, that the fact that my arm rises at the same time as I will it to was mere coincidence. This brings out the contradiction of the Cartesian (referring to Descartes) philosophy, the unresolved dualism, which was its Achilles’ heel.

zh: 尽管存在这些弱点，笛卡尔的哲学仍具有显著的进步性。他在科学领域的突破促进了法国自然科学的发展。在哲学层面，笛卡尔的唯心主义虽被启蒙运动盛行的唯物主义思潮所推翻，但他仍对拉美特利等人产生了影响。而在法国以外，他的思想却成为了两位最伟大的哲学家——斯宾诺莎和莱布尼茨——的起点。
en: Despite its weaknesses, Descartes’ philosophy had a notably progressive side. Its advances in science stimulated the growth of natural science in France. Philosophically, Descartes’ idealism was overthrown by the prevailing materialist trend of the Enlightenment, though he influenced people like La Mettrie. But outside France his ideas were the starting point for two of the greatest philosophers of all, Spinoza and Leibniz.

zh: 斯宾诺莎
en: SPINOZA

zh: 贝内迪克图斯（巴鲁赫）·斯宾诺莎于1632 年出生在阿姆斯特丹，父亲是一位犹太商人，是众多为逃避宗教迫害而从葡萄牙和西班牙逃亡至此的人之一。斯宾诺莎自幼便展现出无畏追求真理的品质，无论后果如何，他都准备捍卫自己的观点。原本他应继承家业，但1656 年，尽管他曾勤勉研读《圣经》和《塔木德》，却与正统拉比们发生了冲突。有人曾以每年1,000 弗罗林为条件要求他保持沉默，但他予以拒绝，并因其“错误观点”和“可怕的异端”而遭到诅咒并被逐出犹太社区。因担心性命不保，他不得不逃离阿姆斯特丹。他定居在莱顿附近的莱茵斯堡，靠打磨透镜谋生，同时利用闲暇时间从事哲学写作。
en: Benedictus (Baruch) Spinoza was born in Amsterdam in 1632, the son of a Jewish merchant, one of many who had fled from Portugal and Spain to escape from religious persecution. From his youth, Spinoza showed himself to be a fearless searcher after truth, prepared to defend his views regardless of the consequences to himself. It was intended that he should carry on the family business, but in 1656, despite having been a diligent student of the Bible and the Talmud, he fell foul of the orthodox rabbis. He was offered 1,000 florins a year to keep silent, but refused and was cursed and expelled from the Jewish community for his “wrong opinions” and “horrible heresies”. Fearing an attempt on his life, he had to flee from Amsterdam. He took up residence at Rijnsburg near Leiden, where he earned his living polishing lenses, while dedicating his spare time to his philosophical writings.

zh: 作为一名被社会排斥的人，斯宾诺莎与一些较小的新教教派成员交好，这些教派与再洗礼派有关联，他们自身也是迫害的受害者，并且对讨论新思想持开放态度。当时，笛卡尔的思想在荷兰正引发一场激烈的争议。1656 年，大学教授被要求宣誓，承诺不会宣扬那些引发争议的笛卡尔思想。在斯宾诺莎周围的小圈子里，笛卡尔被视为灵感的源泉，是一位拒绝仅凭传统来形成观点的勇敢者，他断言我们所知的一切都是通过理性的“自然之光”所认知的。笛卡尔虽给斯宾诺莎带来了启发，但后者拥有过于敏锐的思维，不会不加批判地接受他的观点。
en: As an outcast himself, Spinoza became friendly with the members of some of the smaller Protestant sects, related to the Anabaptists, who were themselves the victims of persecution and who were open to discussions of new ideas. At this time, the ideas of Descartes were the subject of a raging controversy in the Netherlands. In 1656, university professors were required to take an oath that they would not propound Cartesian ideas which caused offence. To the little circle around Spinoza, Descartes was seen as a source of inspiration, as a brave soul who refused to base his opinions on mere tradition, and affirmed that all we know is known by the ‘natural light’ of reason. Descartes was an inspiration to Spinoza, but the latter had too keen an intellect to accept him uncritically.

zh: 这是一个伟大发现的时代。科学正开始展翅高飞，旧有的亚里士多德世界观正被新的科学-机械论的自然观所取代。伽利略本人曾写道，他相信自然的书是用数学语言写成的。斯宾诺莎的整个世界观都贯穿着对自然和科学的热忱。他与英国化学家罗伯特·波义耳保持书信往来，与皇家学会秘书亨利·奥尔登堡讨论彗星，并评论了笛卡尔的运动定律和惠更斯的理论。
en: This was an age of great discoveries. Science was beginning to stretch its wings, and the old Aristotelian world view was being replaced by the new scientific-mechanistic view of nature. Galileo himself had written that he believed that the book of nature was written in the language of mathematics. Spinoza’s whole outlook was dominated by a passionate interest in nature and science. He conducted a correspondence with the English chemist Robert Boyle, discussed comets with Henry Oldenburg, the secretary of the Royal Society, and commented on Descartes’ laws of motion and the theories of Huygens.

zh: 当时，荷兰共和国是欧洲最自由的国家。荷兰资产阶级通过一场革命斗争，在依靠下层中产阶级和半无产阶级群众的支持下，成功地摆脱了西班牙统治的枷锁。1579 年，新教荷兰的北部各省联合起来，组建了乌得勒支联盟，荷兰共和国由此诞生。该联盟的第三条将宗教宽容确立为基本原则。然而，从一开始，这一原则就遭到了强大的“严格”或“严谨”加尔文主义教派的反对，他们只希望在荷兰有一个官方教会——那就是他们自己的教会。
en: The Republic of the Netherlands was the freest country in Europe at this time. The Dutch bourgeoisie had succeeded in throwing off the yoke of Spanish domination by a revolutionary struggle in which it leaned for support on the lower middle class and semi-proletarian masses. In 1579, the Northern provinces of the Protestant Netherlands came together to form the Union of Utrecht, out of which the Dutch Republic emerged. Article Three of the Union proclaimed religious toleration as a basic principle. However, from the outset this was opposed by the powerful sect of ‘strict’ or ‘precise’ Calvinists, who wanted only one official Church in Holland – their own.

zh: 在多德雷赫特宗教会议（1618—1619 年）上，他们成功地使加尔文主义被承认为国教。但自由派的约翰·德·维特——他于1653年至1672年间领导荷兰——坚决反对宗教不容忍。斯宾诺莎并未置身于这场政治斗争之外。他搁置了《伦理学》的撰写工作，转而出版了一本捍卫言论和思想自由的著作——《神学政治论》，该书于1670 年问世。这使他招致了严格加尔文主义者的刻骨仇恨，他们对他试图证明《圣经》不应被视为包含哲学或科学真理的观点感到震惊。
en: At the Synod of Dordrecht (1618-19) they succeeded in getting Calvinism recognised as the official religion. But the liberal Johan de Witt, who was the leader of the Netherlands from 1653 to 1672, stood firm against religious intolerance. Spinoza did not stand aloof from the political struggle. He set aside work on his Ethics in order to publish a book in defence of the freedom of speech and thought, the Treatise on Theology and Politics, which appeared in 1670. This earned him the bitter enmity of the strict Calvinists, who were scandalised by his attempts to show that the Bible is not to be seen as containing philosophical or scientific truths.

zh: 1670 年7 月，教会会议宣布该《神学政治论》是一本“邪恶且亵渎的书”。一份攻击德·维特的匿名小册子将该书描述为“由一个叛教的犹太人与魔鬼在地狱中孕育的产物”，并称其出版是“在约翰·德·维特先生知情的情况下进行的”。
1672 年，法军入侵荷兰共和国，德·维特在海牙被暴民杀害。出于机会主义的考虑，执政官奥兰治的威廉三世站在了加尔文主义者一边。两年后，《神学政治论》一书被禁。在余下的短暂生命中，斯宾诺莎被迫低调行事。令人痛心的是，他的杰作《伦理学》因担心教会的反应，生前从未出版。该书直到1677 年才问世，那一年，这位伟人因肺结核去世。
en: In July 1670, the Synod declared the Treatise an “evil and blasphemous book.” An anonymous pamphlet attacking de Witt described the book as “spawned in Hell by a renegade Jew and the Devil”, and that it was published “with the knowledge of Mr. Johan de Witt”.

In 1672, a French army invaded the Dutch Republic and de Witt was murdered by a mob in The Hague. For opportunist reasons, the stadtholder, William III of Orange, sided with the Calvinists. Two years later the Treatise was banned. For the rest of his short life, Spinoza was forced to keep his head down. Tragically, his masterpiece, the Ethics, was never published in his lifetime, for fear of the reaction of the Church. It only appeared in 1677, the year the great man died of consumption.

zh: 斯宾诺莎是那些在哲学领域掀起真正革命的真正天才之一。他以笛卡尔的哲学为出发点，对其进行了彻底的改造，从而为以真正科学的方式研究自然奠定了基础。“因此值得注意的是，”黑格尔写道，“思想必须首先站在斯宾诺莎主义的立场上；成为斯宾诺莎的追随者，是所有哲学的本质开端。”
不仅黑格尔，歌德、席勒、马克思以及年轻时的谢林也都深受斯宾诺莎的影响。当爱因斯坦与尼尔斯·玻尔就量子力学的根本问题展开哲学争论时，他曾写道，他宁愿请“老斯宾诺莎”来担任仲裁者，也不愿请伯特兰·罗素或鲁道夫·卡纳普。
en: Spinoza was one of those true geniuses who carried out a real revolution in philosophy. Taking as his starting point the philosophy of Descartes, he completely transformed it, and in so doing, laid the basis for a genuinely scientific approach to nature. “It is therefore worthy of note”, wrote Hegel, “that thought must begin by placing itself at the standpoint of Spinozism; to be a follower of Spinoza is the essential commencement of all Philosophy.”

Not only Hegel, but Goethe, Schiller, Marx, and the young Schelling were much influenced by Spinoza. When Einstein was engaged in a philosophical dispute with Niels Bohr over the fundamental problems of quantum mechanics, he wrote that he would rather have ‘old Spinoza’ as a referee instead of Bertrand Russell or Rudolf Carnap.

zh: 也许正因如此，伯特兰·罗素才以他一贯的傲慢态度，在《西方哲学史》中写道，斯宾诺莎的整个“形而上学”是：
en: Maybe that is why, with his customary arrogance, Bertrand Russell, in his History of Western Philosophy, writes that the whole of Spinoza’s “metaphysic” is:

zh: ［它］与现代逻辑和科学方法不相容。事实必须通过观察来发现，而不是通过推理；当我们成功推断未来时，所依据的原理并非逻辑上必然的，而是由经验数据所提示的。而且，斯宾诺莎所依赖的“实体”概念，是当今科学和哲学都无法接受的。
en: [I]ncompatible with modern logic and with scientific method. Facts have to be discovered by observation, not by reasoning; when we successfully infer the future, we do so by means of principles which are not logically necessary, but are suggested by empirical data. And the concept of substance, upon which Spinoza relies, is one which neither science nor philosophy can nowadays accept.

zh: 关键在于，斯宾诺莎没有将自己局限于经验哲学的狭隘范畴，因而能够超越当时机械论科学的局限。当贝克莱和休谟将哲学引向死胡同时（如果科学曾听从他们的意见——所幸并未如此——科学也会步其后尘），斯宾诺莎却以卓越的智慧指明了前进的方向。尽管罗素及其逻辑实证主义同道们提出了荒谬的自命不凡——他们毫无依据地自诩为由自己任意定义的所谓“科学方法”的至高守护者——但科学的发展方式与上述论述所指出的大相径庭。
en: The whole point is that Spinoza, by not restricting himself to the narrow confines of empirical philosophy, was able to transcend the limits of the mechanistic science of the day. While Berkeley and Hume led philosophy into a blind alley (and they would have done the same to science, had it paid any attention to them, which fortunately it did not), Spinoza brilliantly showed the way forward. In spite of the ridiculous pretensions of Russell and his fellow logical positivists, who – without the slightest basis – put themselves forward as the supreme guardians of an alleged ‘scientific method’ arbitrarily defined by themselves, science proceeds in an entirely different way to that indicated in these lines.

zh: 特别是，伟大假说在引导科学研究走向正确方向方面发挥了至关重要的作用。而且，根据定义，一个假说只能基于数量有限的“事实”。它必须包含推理，同时也需要勇气和想象力。例如，如果科学家们当初重视康德关于太阳系起源的星云说，本可以节省多少时间和精力？反过来说，如今在寻找“冷暗物质”的过程中又浪费了多少时间——这种物质既没有任何“观测事实”作为依据，其目的却在于支持一种比斯宾诺莎所设想的任何事物都更离奇的宇宙学假说。
en: In particular, the role of great hypotheses in pointing scientific research in the right direction has been fundamental. And, by definition, a hypothesis can only be based on a limited number of ‘facts’. It must involve reasoning, and also courage and imagination. How much time and effort would have been saved if scientists had paid attention to Kant’s nebular theory of the origin of the solar system, for example? On the other hand, how much time is now being wasted in the search for ‘cold, dark matter’, which is based upon no ‘observed facts’ whatsoever, and which is intended to support a cosmological hypothesis more fantastic than anything Spinoza ever thought of.

zh: 那个时代的哲学之所以备受赞誉，正在于它没有被当时自然知识的局限所误导，而且——从斯宾诺莎到伟大的法国唯物主义者——它坚持从世界本身来解释世界，并将详细的论证留给未来的自然科学。
en: It is to the highest credit of the philosophy of the time that it did not let itself be led astray by the restricted state of contemporary natural knowledge, and that – from Spinoza down to the great French materialists – it insisted on explaining the world from the world itself and left the justification in detail to the natural science of the future.

zh: 斯宾诺莎凭借理性的力量，仅凭当时极为有限的科学成果，便提出了有史以来最伟大的假说之一。他与笛卡尔决裂——后者主张“无灵魂的身体”与“无身体的灵魂”——进而提出，身体与心灵是同一事物的两个属性。宇宙并非如笛卡尔二元论所宣称的那样由心灵和物质组成。只有一个实体，它自身包含了思想与存在的所有属性。它是无限的、永恒的，并拥有产生我们所见宇宙中丰富现象的一切潜能。
en: Spinoza, by the strength of reason, and with the very limited scientific results available to him, arrived at one of the greatest hypotheses of all time. Breaking with Descartes, with his notion of a body without a soul and a soul without a body, he advanced the idea that body and mind are two attributes of one and the same thing. The universe is not composed of mind and matter, as alleged by Descartes’ dualism. There is only a single Substance, which contains within itself all the attributes of thought and being. It is infinite and eternal, and possesses all the potential to give rise to the abundance of phenomena we see in the universe.

zh: 斯宾诺莎将这一实体命名为“上帝”。但实际上，将上帝等同于自然，就等于废除了上帝——斯宾诺莎的对手们在指责他无神论时，对此心知肚明。在斯宾诺莎的宇宙中，它是无限的、永恒的，因此既非被创造的，也不受天堂或地狱的束缚，其中没有独立神明的容身之地。事实上，除了实体之外，没有任何事物能存在于其中——而实体不过是自然的另一种表述方式。
en: Spinoza gives this Substance the name of “God”. But in reality, to make God equal to nature is to abolish God – a fact which was not lost on Spinoza’s enemies when they accused him of atheism. In Spinoza’s universe, infinite and eternal, and therefore uncreated and unbounded by heaven or hell, there is no room for a separate deity. Indeed, there is no room for anything whatsoever except Substance, which is just another way of saying nature.

zh: 因此，从某种奇特的角度来看，斯宾诺莎的哲学尽管表面上具有唯心主义的外观，却是在辩证意义上（即非机械意义上）的唯物主义真正的出发点。只需将“上帝”一词替换为“物质”，我们便得到一个完全自洽的唯物主义立场。正如马克思在1858 年5 月31 日致拉萨尔的信中写道：
en: Thus, in a strange way, the philosophy of Spinoza, despite its idealist appearance, is the real point of departure for materialism in the dialectical, that is, non-mechanical sense of the word. All that is necessary is to substitute the word ‘matter’ for ‘God’ and we get a perfectly consistent materialist position. As Marx wrote in a letter to Lassalle on 31 May 1858:

zh: 即使对于那些将自己的著作系统化了的哲学家——例如斯宾诺莎——该体系的真正内在结构也与他有意识地呈现的形式大相径庭。
en: Even in the case of philosophers who give systematic form to their work, Spinoza for instance, the true inner structure of the system is quite unlike the form in which it was consciously presented by him.

zh: 马克思和恩格斯对斯宾诺莎的崇高敬意由普列汉诺夫揭示出来，他回忆起1889 年与当时已年迈的恩格斯的一次谈话：
en: The great admiration of Marx and Engels for Spinoza was revealed by Plekhanov, who recalls a conversation he had with Engels, by then an old man, in 1889:

zh: “那么你认为，”我问道，“老斯宾诺莎说‘思想和广延不过是同一个实体的两个属性’，这种说法对吗？”“当然，”恩格斯回答道，“老斯宾诺莎是完全正确的。”
en: “So do you think”, I asked, “old Spinoza was right when he said that thought and extent are nothing but two attributes of one and the same substance?” “Of course,” Engels replied, “old Spinoza was quite right.”

zh: 物质宇宙的存在被视为一个公理。斯宾诺莎的范式是几何学，它以公理为出发点：这些“不言自明”的断言无需证明。然而，那些愿意不加质疑地接受欧几里得公理（顺便说一句，这些公理远非不言自明的真理，反而面临着严重的质疑）的人，却对承认物质世界的现实性表现出极度的抗拒，声称这超出了我们知识的范畴，无法断言。然而，正是这个物质世界，才是我们一切经验和知识的起点。“上帝，或者说由各种属性构成的实体——其中每一项属性都表达着永恒且无限的本质——必然存在”，斯宾诺莎如是宣称。
此外，物质既不能被创造，也不能被毁灭，只能发生变化：
en: The existence of the material universe is taken as an axiom. The model for Spinoza was geometry, which sets out with axioms: ‘self-evident’ assertions which require no proof. Yet the same people who are prepared to accept on trust the axioms of Euclid (which, incidentally, far from being self-evident truths, are open to serious objections) nevertheless display extreme reluctance to admit the reality of the material world, declaring this to be beyond our knowledge to assert. However, this same material world is the starting point of all our experience and knowledge. “God or a substance consisting of attributes, each of which expresses eternal and infinite essence, necessarily exists”, proclaims Spinoza.
Moreover, matter can neither be created nor destroyed, only changed:

zh: 物质在任何地方都是一样的，其各部分之间并无区别，除非我们认为物质以各种方式受到影响；由此，其各部分在样式上相互区别，但在现实中并不区别。例如，我们可以将水——就其作为水而言——理解为可被分割且其各部分彼此分离；但就其作为物体性实体而言则不然，因为此时它既未被分离也未被分割。同样，水就其作为水而言，可以被创造和毁灭；但就其作为实体而言，既不能被创造，也不能被毁灭。
en: Matter is the same everywhere, and its parts are not distinguished one from the other except in so far as we conceive matter to be affected in various ways, whence its parts are distinguished one from the other modally but not in reality. E.g., we can conceive water, in so far as it is water, to be divided and its parts separated one from the other: but not in so far as it is corporeal substance, for then it is neither separated nor divided. Again, water, in so far as it is water, can be made and destroyed, but in so far as it is substance it can neither be made nor destroyed.

zh: 因此，上帝并不存在于物质世界之外，而物质世界并未被创造，因为它始终存在。他是“自由”的——自由地遵循自然法则，等等。换言之，“上帝”即自然本身。斯宾诺莎的这种泛神论实际上是一种伪装得并不高明的唯物主义。尽管其形式颇为独特（这或许是试图抵御无神论指控却未果的尝试），但这远比同时代科学家的机械论观点高明得多。与物质受外部力量驱动的机械论观念不同，这里所说的物质是按照其自身固有的规律运动的，它是“其自身的原因”。
en: God thus has no existence separate and apart from the material world, which has not been created because it has always existed. He is ‘free’ – to obey the laws of nature, and so on. In other words, ‘God’ is only nature. This pantheism of Spinoza is really a thinly-disguised materialism. Despite its peculiar form (probably an unsuccessful attempt to ward off accusations of atheism), this is head and shoulders above the mechanistic outlook of contemporary scientists. Instead of the mechanical conception of matter being moved by an external force, here we have matter which moves according to its own inherent laws, it is ‘its own cause’.

zh: 思想若脱离实体（物质）便无法存在。它是以某种特定方式组织起来的物质所具有的属性，“因此，思维实体与广延实体是同一个实体，时而通过这个属性，时而通过那个属性来理解它。”换言之，思想与物质是“同一事物，只是以两种方式表现出来”。
这确实是一个重大突破。本质上，这里对思想与存在之间的关系做出了正确的评估；并非像笛卡尔那样将二者彻底分离，而是将其视为辩证的统一体。不是思想与物质对立，而是会思考的物质。在此，斯宾诺莎接近于一种公开的唯物主义立场：他说：“心灵只有在感知身体各种变化的观念时，才认识自身。”。
他还指出：“因为人的身体……以多种方式受到外部物体的影响，也倾向于以多种方式影响外部物体。但人的心灵……必须感知发生在人体内的一切事物。”
en: Thought can have no existence apart from Substance (matter). It is an attribute of matter organised in a certain way, “consequently thinking substance and extended substance are one and the same substance, which is comprehended through this and now through that attribute.” In other words, thought and matter are “one and the same thing, but expressed in two ways”.

This is a real breakthrough. In essence, we have here a correct assessment of the relation between thought and being; not, as in Descartes, a radical separation of the two, but their dialectical unity. Not thought opposed to matter, but matter that thinks. Here, Spinoza comes close to an overtly materialist position: “The mind”, he says, “has no knowledge of itself save in so far as it perceives the ideas of the modifications of the body”.

And again: “For the human body … is affected by external bodies in many ways and disposed to affect external bodies in many ways. But the human mind … must perceive all things which happen in the human body.”

zh: 这种论述远胜于机械唯物主义那种粗鄙的观念——后者将思想视为大脑分泌的一种物质，就像汗腺分泌的汗水一样。斯宾诺莎追随笛卡尔的观点，指出思想与物质的区别在于它没有广延。它不是物质，而是大脑本身的功能，是其本质属性。思想不仅仅是一种抽象的沉思活动，更是思考者以有意识的方式对其环境作出反应的方式。思想无法与人类的其他所有活动相分离。正如斯宾诺莎所理解的，思想是高度组织化的物质——即“会思考的自然”——的一种属性，而非与自然相对立的事物：
en: This presentation was far superior to the crude conception of mechanical materialism which saw thought as a material substance secreted from the brain, like sweat from the sweat glands. Spinoza, following Descartes, says that thought differs from matter in that it has no extension. It is not a material thing, but the very function of the brain itself, its essential property. Thought is not merely an abstract contemplative activity, but the way in which thinking beings react to their environment at the conscious level. It is not possible to separate thought from all other human activities. Thought, as Spinoza understood, is one of the attributes of highly organised matter, nature that thinks, and not something opposed to nature:

zh: 如果真是这样，那么意识与自然、思维与存在、思维规律与自然规律之间竟如此紧密地对应，这无疑显得极为奇怪。但如果我们进而追问思想和意识究竟是什么、从何而来，就会发现它们是人类大脑的产物，而人类本身也是自然的产物，是在环境中并随着环境的发展而形成的；由此不难看出，人类大脑的产物——归根结底也是自然的产物——并不与自然界的其他相互联系相矛盾，而是与之相契合。
en: If this were so, it must seem most odd that consciousness and nature, thinking and being, the laws of thought and the laws of nature, should so closely correspond. But if we then ask what thought and consciousness are and whence they come, we find that they are products of the human brain and that man himself is a product of nature, who has developed in and along with his environment; whence it is self-evident that the products of the human brain, which in the last analysis are also products of nature, do not contradict the rest of nature’s interconnections but correspond to them.

zh: 在此，思想与物质虽有区别，但并非机械对立、互斥的对立面。斯宾诺莎认识到，物质（“实体”）本身就包含着产生思想所需的一切要素。只要各种因素以恰当的方式相互关联，无机物质便会演化出有机物质。甚至最原始的生命形式也能进化为具有思维能力的生物。并不像笛卡尔所认为的那样，存在一条将有机物质与无机物质、或人类与动物绝对分隔开的界线。在所有这些思想中，斯宾诺莎都展现出了远超其时代的远见。
en: Here thought and matter are different but not mechanically opposed, mutually exclusive opposites. Spinoza understood that matter (“Substance”) contains within itself all that is necessary to give rise to thought. Given the right concatenation of factors, organic matter arises out of inorganic matter. And even the most primitive life forms can evolve to produce thinking beings. There is not, as Descartes thought, an absolute dividing line separating organic from inorganic matter, or man from the animals. In all these ideas, Spinoza showed himself to be far in advance of his times.

zh: 斯宾诺莎认为，征服自然和完善人类是追求知识的主要目的。在伦理与道德领域，他也倡导了非常先进的思想。他正确地认识到，道德是相对的：
en: Spinoza believed that mastery over nature and the improvement of man were the main purpose of the pursuit of knowledge. In the field of ethics and morality too, he defends very advanced ideas. He correctly understood that morality was relative:

zh: 至于“善”与“恶”这两个术语，就事物本身而言，它们也并不表示事物本身的任何实在性质，它们只不过是思维的方式，或是我们通过将事物相互比较而形成的观念。因为同一事物可以同时是好的、坏的，也可以是无所谓的。例如，音乐对忧郁者来说是好的，对哀悼者来说是坏的，对聋子来说则既非好也非坏。尽管如此，我们仍必须保留这些词语。
en: As for the terms good and bad, they also mean nothing positive in things considered in themselves, nor are they anything else than modes of thought, or notions, which we form from the comparison of things with each other. For one and the same thing can at the same time be good, bad, and indifferent. E.g., music is good to the melancholy, bad to those who mourn, and neither good nor bad to the deaf. Although this be so, these words must be retained by us.

zh: 他否定了自由意志的观念，转而主张一种彻底的决定论立场。不存在所谓的“自由”行为，因为所有行为都有其原因，无论我们是否意识到这一点。斯宾诺莎是第一个对自由与必然性之间的关系进行辩证评价的人，他指出，真正的自由在于对必然性的理解。真正的自由并不在于否认客观自然规律的存在，而在于努力理解这些规律，从而掌握它们。
en: He rejected the idea of free will, and instead advocated a thoroughly determinist position. There are no ‘free’ actions, in the sense that all actions are caused by something, whether we are aware of it or not. Spinoza was the first one to give a dialectical appraisal of the relation between freedom and necessity, when he pointed out that real freedom consists in the understanding of necessity. True freedom does not consist in denying the existence of the objective laws of nature, but in striving to understand them in order to gain mastery over them.

zh: 他无论在何处发现偏见和迷信，都会予以反对，并且早在法国启蒙运动之前，就决定将所有偏见都召至“理性的法庭”受审。对于那些躲藏在“无知的避难所”——上帝意志之中的人，他除了蔑视之外别无他感。在以下这段话中，他无疑是基于痛苦的亲身经历而发出的感叹：
en: He opposed prejudice and superstition wherever he found them and, long before the French Enlightenment, decided to summon all prejudices to the “court of reason”. For those who take refuge in the will of God, “the asylum of ignorance”, he has nothing but contempt. In the following passage, he was undoubtedly speaking from painful personal experience:

zh: 因此，当他们看到人体时，又会感到惊叹；由于他们不知道如此精妙的造物之因，便断定这并非机械技艺所为，而是神圣或超自然的技艺所为，且构造得使得各部分互不伤害。因此，凡是想要探究奇迹的真正原因，像学者一样理解自然之事，而不是像傻瓜一样惊愕地盯着它们的人，都会被广泛视为异端和不虔诚，并被那些被民众奉为自然与诸神解释者的人所指责。
en: Thus again, when they see the human body they are amazed, and as they know not the cause of so much art, they conclude that it was made not by mechanical art, but divine or supernatural art, and constructed in such a manner that one part does not injure another. And hence it comes about that someone who wishes to seek out the true causes of miracles, and to understand the things of nature like a man of learning, and not stare at them in amazement like a fool, is widely deemed heretical and impious, and proclaimed such by those whom the mob adore as the interpreters of nature and the Gods.

zh: 斯宾诺莎哲学的基本思想是一元论——即万物归一。存在的万千形态、形状、色彩、运动形式，不过是同一“实体”的不同表现，该实体能够呈现出无限多样的形式。他将这些偶然的、暂时的现象称为“样式”（modi，单数形式为modus）。它们是物质所呈现的形式，如同浩瀚海洋上永不停息的波涛，不断产生又消逝。但这些转瞬即逝的存在形式无法脱离实体而独立存在——实体是无边无际且永恒的，它遵循自身的法则运作，必然会产生无数具体的、有限的形式。而这些形式本身并非自由的行动者，而是受制于决定万物存在的自然法则。借助理性的力量，我们能够理解这些法则，从而获得自由，有意识地决定我们的行动，并领悟我们在宇宙中的真实位置。
en: The basic idea of Spinoza’s philosophy is monism – the idea that all things are one. All the myriad forms of existence, the shapes, colours, forms of movement, are only different expressions of the same Substance, which can assume an infinite variety of forms. These accidental, temporary phenomena he calls ‘modi’ (singular, modus). They are the forms which matter assumes, continually coming into being and disappearing, like the restless waves on a mighty ocean. But these transitory forms of being can have no separate existence independent from Substance, which is unbounded and eternal, and which, operating according to its own laws, must give rise to an unlimited number of particular, finite forms. These forms, in turn, are not free agents, but subject to natural laws which determine the existence of all things. Through the agency of reason, it is possible to understand these laws and thereby achieve freedom consciously to determine our actions and comprehend our true place in the universe.

zh: 这一宏伟的哲学与现代科学的发现完全一致。我们在宇宙中看到的有机和无机物质的无穷无尽的形式，都可以归结为同一种实体——分子、原子和亚原子粒子。根据现代物理学，少数夸克以不同的方式组合，形成数百种强子，这些强子又结合起来构成约一百种化学元素的原子核。它们与轻子共同构成原子，原子进而结合形成分子，而万物皆由分子构成。因此，宇宙中所有存在形式的基础都是同一种物质。当然，这一图景比斯宾诺莎描绘的要复杂得多——当时他所依据的信息极其有限。在科学取得长足进步之前，他的宇宙图景无法得到充分证实。但他提出的“万物源于同一物质”这一假说，在很大程度上已得到证实。
en: This imposing philosophy is in complete accord with the discoveries of modern science. All the endless forms of organic and inorganic matter we see in the universe can be reduced to the same substance – molecules, atoms and subatomic particles. According to modern physics, a small number of quarks are put together in different ways to make hundreds of hadrons, which combine to form the nuclei of a hundred or so chemical elements. Together with leptons, they then make up atoms, which then combine to make molecules, out of which everything else is built. The same material substance therefore underlies all the forms of being in the universe. Of course, this picture is much more complicated than the one painted by Spinoza, who had only the scantiest of information to go on. A long period of scientific advance was necessary before his picture of the universe could be properly corroborated. But his hypothesis that everything comes from a common substance has been substantially vindicated.

zh: 一元论原则既可以从唯物主义的角度，也可以从唯心主义的角度来解释。柏拉图和黑格尔也是一元论者，因为他们认为宇宙及其中的万物归根结底是“绝对理念”的体现。马克思和恩格斯则是唯物主义的一元论者。斯宾诺莎的情况则较为特殊。虽然从形式上讲他必须被视为唯心论者，但他的“实体”概念中存在某种模糊性，这无疑为唯物主义的解释留下了空间。这一点很快就被他的同时代人——无论是犹太人还是基督徒——所察觉，他们因此指控他无神论。各种骇人听闻的罪行和不道德的思想都被归咎于他。在他去世后的很长一段时间里，上流社会几乎不敢提及他的名字。德国作家莱辛曾说，在他那个时代——即一个世纪之后——人们对待斯宾诺莎“就像对待一条死狗一样”。
en: The principle of monism can be interpreted either in a materialist or an idealist sense. Plato and Hegel were also monists, because they considered that the universe and everything in it was ultimately an expression of the Absolute Idea. Marx and Engels were materialist monists. Spinoza’s case is peculiar. While formally he has to be considered an idealist, there is an element of ambiguity about his Substance which is certainly open to a materialist interpretation. This was quickly grasped by his contemporaries, Jews and Christians alike, who accused him of atheism. All kinds of heinous crimes and immoral ideas were attributed to him. For a long time after his death his name could hardly be mentioned in polite society. The German writer Lessing said that, in his day, a century later, people treated Spinoza ‘like a dead dog’.

zh: 尽管遭受了种种诽谤，斯宾诺莎的哲学依然作为一座丰碑，见证了孕育它的伟大而崇高的精神。他的哲学非常接近唯物主义，这不可避免地使他得出了最先进的社会结论，这与休谟和贝克莱那反动的厌弃人类的思想形成了鲜明对比。这一点在他杰作《伦理学》的篇章中表现得十分清楚：
en: Despite all the calumnies, Spinoza’s philosophy stands as a monument to the great and noble spirit that conceived it. His philosophy, which came very close to materialism, inevitably led him to draw the most advanced social conclusions, in contrast to the reactionary misanthropy of Hume and Berkeley. This comes across clearly in the pages of his masterpiece, Ethics:

zh: 人对人而言即为神。然而，人们极少在理性的指引下生活，反而在彼此之间，世事往往演变为彼此嫉妒或相互骚扰。然而，他们几乎无法过独居生活，因此对许多人而言，将人定义为“社会性动物”这一说法极具吸引力；事实上，世事本就如此安排：人类共同生活所带来的便利远多于不便。因此，让讽刺家们尽情嘲笑人间事务吧，让神学家们诋毁它们吧，也让忧郁者们尽可能地赞美那种粗野而未经教养的生活：让他们鄙视人类、推崇野兽——尽管如此，人类仍将通过经验发现：通过互助，他们能更轻松地获得所需之物；通过联合力量，也能更轻松地避开四面八方的危险；更不用说，关注人类的作为而非野兽的行径，是多么优越，也更值得我们去了解。
en: Man is a God to man. Yet it rarely happens that men live under the guidance of reason, but among them things are in such a state that they are usually envious of or a nuisance to each other. But nevertheless they are scarcely able to lead a solitary life, so that to many the definition of man as a social animal has been very attractive; and in truth things are so ordered that from the common society of men far more conveniences arise than the contrary. Let satirists therefore laugh to their hearts’ content at human affairs, let theologians revile them, and let the melancholy praise as much as they can the rude and uncultivated life: let them despise men and admire the brutes – despite all this, men will find by experience that they can procure with mutual aid far more easily what they need, and avoid far more easily the perils which beset them on all sides, by united forces: to say nothing of how much better it is, and more worthy of our knowledge, to regard the deeds of men rather than those of the brutes.

zh: 莱布尼茨
en: LEIBNIZ

zh: 在一粒沙中看见一个世界，
在一朵野花中看见一片天堂，
把无限握在你的掌心，
将永恒容于一小时。
威廉·布莱克，《纯真预言》
en: To see a World in a Grain of Sand,
And a heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand,
And Eternity in an hour.
William Blake, Auguries of Innocence

zh: 斯宾诺莎的一元论观点遭到了他那位伟大的同时代人戈特弗里德·莱布尼茨（1646—1716）的挑战，后者同样是一位博学多才的学者。莱布尼茨身兼数学家、物理学家、地质学家、生物学家、外交官、图书馆员和历史学家等多重身份。他发明了微积分，尽管牛顿声称自己更早便已发明。在物理学领域，他预见了能量守恒定律。他还被视为数学逻辑的奠基人，尽管他并未发表过关于该主题的著作。
en: The monist views of Spinoza were challenged by his great contemporary, Gottfried Leibniz (1646-1716), yet another encyclopaedic mind. Leibniz was a mathematician, physicist, geologist, biologist, diplomat, librarian, and historian. He invented infinitesimal calculus, although Newton claimed to have done this earlier. In physics, he anticipated the law of preservation of energy. He is also considered to have been the founder of mathematical logic, although he did not publish his work on this subject.

zh: 尽管莱布尼茨是一位客观唯心主义者，但他仍发展了辩证法。列宁在《哲学笔记》中写道：“莱布尼茨通过神学得出了物质与运动不可分割（且普遍、绝对）的联系这一原则。”
马克思也表达了对莱布尼茨的钦佩之情。

斯宾诺莎哲学的基础是单一的普遍实体。莱布尼茨同样从实体的概念出发，但对其定义有所不同。他将实体视为一种生命活动、内在运动和能量。与斯宾诺莎的根本区别在于：斯宾诺莎强调存在的单一性，而莱布尼茨则将全部重点放在宇宙的多样性上。对他而言，整个宇宙由无数实体组成，他称之为“单子”。莱布尼茨的单子与原子概念相似。在巴黎期间，莱布尼茨结识了唯物主义者伽森狄并受到其影响，后者曾重新唤起了人们对德谟克利特和伊壁鸠鲁原子论哲学的兴趣。对莱布尼茨而言，万物皆由单子构成，包括我们自身。然而，这一理论存在一些独特之处。首先，没有两个单子是相同的。每个单子都是一个独立的特殊世界，外界无法穿透。莱布尼茨认为，世上没有两样事物是完全相同的。每个单子（且其数量是无限的）也是一个小宇宙，反映着整个宇宙。它是万物总体的某种胚胎。因此，个别包含普遍。
en: An objective idealist, Leibniz nevertheless developed dialectics. In his Philosophical Notebooks, Lenin wrote that “Leibniz through theology arrived at the principle of the inseparable (and universal, absolute) connection of matter and motion.”
Marx also expressed his admiration for Leibniz.

The basis of Spinoza’s philosophy was the single universal substance. Leibniz also starts from the notion of substance but defines it differently. He sees it like living activity, internal motion, and energy. The fundamental difference with Spinoza is that, where he stressed the singleness of being, Leibniz lays all the emphasis on the multiplicity of the universe. For him, the entire universe is composed of an infinite number of substances which he calls ‘monads’. The monads of Leibniz are similar to the idea of atoms. Whilst in Paris, Leibniz met and was influenced by the materialist Gassendi, who had revived interest in the atomistic philosophy of Democritus and Epicurus. For Leibniz, everything is made of monads, including ourselves. However, there are some peculiarities in this theory. To begin with, no monad is like another. Each is its own special world, impenetrable from without. Leibniz thought that no two things in the world were the same. Each monad (and there are an infinite number of them) is also a microcosm, which reflects the universe at large. It is a kind of embryo of the totality of things. Thus, the particular contains the universal.

zh: 整个宇宙不过是所有单子的总和。万物都是单子的集合，甚至包括人的灵魂。此外，这些单子并非死物，而是充满生命活力的中心，处于不断的运动与变化之中。从许多方面来看，这一图景惊人地预见了现代原子论的宇宙观。莱布尼茨的想法很可能源于通过显微镜的观察。因此，他将物体比作一个鱼塘：其中最微小的水滴都充满生机，尽管不能说鱼塘本身是活的。费尔巴哈将斯宾诺莎的哲学比作望远镜——它使那些因距离遥远而肉眼不可见的物体变得可见；而莱布尼茨的哲学则像显微镜——它使那些因极其微小而难以察觉的物体变得可见。单子就像一个单独的细胞，其中包含构建整个身体所需的所有信息。同样，在《资本论》中，马克思从一个单独的细胞——商品——推导出资本主义的所有矛盾。
en: The entire universe is only the sum total of all the monads. Everything is an aggregate of monads, even the human soul. Moreover, these monads are not dead matter, but centres of living activity, in constant movement and mutation. In many respects, this picture is a striking anticipation of the modern atomistic view of the universe. Leibniz most likely got his idea from observations through a microscope. Thus, he compares bodies to a fish pond in which the smallest drop of water is full of teeming life, although it cannot be said that the pond itself lives. Feuerbach compared Spinoza’s philosophy to a telescope which makes objects visible to the human eye that are otherwise invisible because of their remoteness, whereas that of Leibniz is like a microscope which makes objects visible that are unnoticeable because of their minuteness and fineness. A monad is like an individual cell which contains all the information required to construct an entire body. In the same way, in Capital, Marx derives all the contradictions of capitalism from a single cell, the commodity.

zh: 尽管其形式带有唯心主义色彩，但其中蕴含着深刻思想的萌芽，以及一种基于运动、无限联系、变化以及从低级阶段向高级阶段演化的自然辩证概念。例如，他区分了不同层次的单子：从最低等级——类似于无机自然的阶段，在此阶段，单子的生命仅以运动的形式表现出来。还有更高层次，类似于植物、动物，最终达到人类灵魂的阶段。“这是一种辩证法，”列宁评论道，“尽管带有唯心主义和教权主义色彩，但非常深刻。”
上帝在单子中扮演什么角色？看来并不大。莱布尼茨将上帝视为所有单子的“充分理由”。费尔巴哈认为他只是半个基督徒、无神论者，或是基督徒与自然主义者的混合体。正如施韦格勒所言：“对莱布尼茨而言，在不放弃两者的前提条件下，将他的单子论与有神论协调统一起来，是一件困难的事。”
en: Despite its idealistic form, there is here the germ of a profound idea and a dialectical concept of nature, based on movement, infinite connections, change and evolution from a lower to a higher stage. For example, he distinguishes between different levels of monads, from the lowest rank, analogous to the stage of inorganic nature, in which the life of the monads expresses itself only in the form of motion. There are higher stages, analogous to plants, animals, which culminates in the human soul. “Here is dialectics of a kind”, commented Lenin, “and very profound, despite the idealism and clericalism.”

What role does God have in relation to the monads? Not very much, it seems. Leibniz makes God the “sufficient reason” of all the monads. Feuerbach considered him to be only half a Christian, atheist, or a cross between a Christian and a naturalist. As Schwegler remarks: “It was a hard matter for Leibniz to bring – without abandoning the presuppositions of both – his monadology and his Theism into unison.”

zh: 从客观唯心主义的立场来看，莱布尼茨的认识论与洛克的经验主义相对立。莱布尼茨可被视为德国唯心主义之父。他最著名的学说当属“最优可能世界”学说，该学说认为，不可能存在比现存世界更完美的世界。对于莱布尼茨效力的那些富裕贵族而言，这无疑是一种令人欣慰的想法。但从哲学角度来看，他们的这种满足感其实并无充分依据。在莱布尼茨看来，虽然存在无穷多的可能世界，但只有一个被上帝选中。换言之，我们此刻所生活的世界之所以是“最好的”，仅仅是因为它是唯一的。然而，同一位莱布尼茨在其《单子论》第22 节中写道：“简单实体的每一个当下状态都是其先前状态的自然结果，其当下状态已蕴含了其未来。”
en: Leibniz’s theory of knowledge is in opposition to the empiricism of Locke from the standpoint of objective idealism. Leibniz may be considered the father of German idealism. He is best known for his famous doctrine of “the best of all possible worlds”, according to which it is impossible that there should be any more perfect a world than that which exists. This must have been a comforting thought for the wealthy aristocrats for whom Leibniz worked. But from a philosophical standpoint, their satisfaction would not really be justified. For Leibniz, there are an infinite number of possible worlds, but only one has been chosen by God. In other words, the world we live in at this particular moment is the “best” one because it is the only one. However, the same Leibniz writes in his Monadology number 22: “Every present state of a simple substance is the natural consequence of its preceding state, in such a way that its present is big with its future.”

zh: 莱布尼茨的辩证哲学既呼应了赫拉克利特，又预示了黑格尔，它绝非在捍卫一成不变的现状，“因为所有物体都像河流一样处于永恒的流变之中，其组成部分也在不断地涌入或流逝。”
en: Leibniz’s dialectical philosophy, which echoes Heraclitus and anticipates Hegel, was far from defending the idea of an unchanging status quo, “because all bodies are in a state of perpetual flux like rivers, and the parts are continually entering in or passing out.”

zh: 在笛卡尔、斯宾诺莎和莱布尼茨的著作中，我们可以看到基于科学发展所得出的卓越结论。然而，这些成就却因当时科学仍从属于传统哲学而受到制约。费尔巴哈洞察到了这些思想家著作中的这一矛盾，他指出：“莱布尼茨和笛卡尔仅在一般意义上属于唯心主义者，但涉及具体事物时，他们却是唯物主义者。”
为了使科学——以及随之而来的哲学——得以进步，它必须摆脱所谓“自然哲学”和“形而上学”的束缚，从而使思想从思辨的领域转向实践的领域。特奥多尔·奥伊泽曼评论道：
en: In the works of Descartes, Spinoza and Leibniz, we see brilliant conclusions reached on the basis of the developments in science. These achievements, however, were held back by the fact that science at this stage remained subordinate to traditional philosophy. Feuerbach grasped this contradiction in the works of these men when he said that: “Leibniz and Descartes are idealists only in a general sense, but when it comes to particular things they are materialists.”

For science to advance – and with it philosophy – it had to release itself from what was known as Natural Philosophy and Metaphysics, so that thought could go from the realm of speculation to the realm of practice. Teodor Oizerman commented:

zh: 笛卡尔、莱布尼茨和斯宾诺莎的理性主义体系，尽管包含各种神学假设，却与实证科学息息相关。十七世纪的形而上学“在数学、物理学及其他精确科学中做出了发现，这些发现似乎属于其研究范畴。这种表象早在十八世纪初就被消除了。实证科学脱离了形而上学，划定了自己的独立领域。正当现实存在与世间事物开始成为所有关注的中心之时，形而上学的全部财富却仅剩思想中的存在与天界之事。”
因此，形而上学（主要是唯心主义）体系与实证科学之间的联系，绝非源于唯心主义的本质，而是源于实证科学当时尚未从哲学中分离出来这一事实。但当这一过程基本完成后，人们发现，那些声称能够认识某种超物理现实并建立起一个封闭的、完美的知识体系的形而上学体系，与日益集中于现实生活和世俗问题的科学知识的实际发展发生了冲突。这些形而上学体系因此声名狼藉，并被十八世纪法国的唯物主义所击败。
en: The rationalistic systems of Descartes, Leibniz, and Spinoza, for all their theological assumptions, were related to the positive sciences. Seventeenth-century metaphysics “made discoveries in mathematics, physics and other exact sciences which seemed to come within its scope. This semblance was done away with as early as the beginning of the eighteenth century. The positive sciences broke away from metaphysics and marked out their independent fields. The whole wealth of metaphysics now consisted only of beings of thought and heavenly things, at the very time when real beings and earthly things began to be the centre of all interest.”

So, the connection between the metaphysical (mainly idealistic) systems and the positive sciences did not at all spring from the nature of idealism but from the fact that the positive sciences had yet to separate from philosophy. But when this process was in the main complete, it transpired that the metaphysical systems, with their claim to knowledge of some super-physical reality and the establishment of a closed system of perfect knowledge, ran into conflict with the actual development of scientific knowledge, which increasingly concentrated on vital, terrestrial problems. The metaphysical systems were discredited and were vanquished by French eighteenth-century materialism.
